extracted.intended_audience: Journal Editors (Editors-in-Chief, Handling/Associate/Section Editors) at Springer Nature journals
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for journal editors at Springer Nature covering editorial practice, peer review, ethical oversight, conflicts of interest, and handling of complaints and post-publication issues. Intended to guide Editors-in-Chief and handling editors in ensuring the quality and integrity of published research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall responsibility for quality and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor-in-Chief is responsible for guaranteeing, as far as possible, the quality and ethics of everything that is published in the journal; Handling Editors should also take responsibility for ensuring the quality of manuscripts which are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Editors work to maintain the highest standards of editorial practice and follow the Publisher's framework of policies, processes and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Springer Nature Code of Conduct and COPE Core Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors follow the minimum standards as set out in the Springer Nature Code of Conduct for Editors and are expected to follow the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) Core Practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with publication and research ethics issues, Editors are expected to follow COPE guidance and flowcharts or any guidance provided by Springer Nature. The final course of action should be decided by the Editors; in difficult cases they may seek advice from the Publisher and collaborate where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of journal editorial policies and author information
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to be aware of the editorial policies and information provided for authors by the Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global inclusion and diversity in editorial composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor-in-Chief should appoint a team of editorial stakeholders and try to ensure that the composition of the team is diverse in terms of expertise and seniority and drawn from the diverse and global research communities served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting peer reviewers, Editors should try to engage reviewers from a diverse pool to seek a balanced point of view while ensuring reviewers have appropriate subject knowledge and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with journal peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to comply with the Journal’s peer review policy (e.g. open, single-blind, double-blind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review aims to assess the validity of the reported research and suitability for the journal’s scope and aims; Editors must ensure manuscripts reporting primary research are peer reviewed by competent reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts reporting primary research or secondary analysis should be peer reviewed by reviewers who are competent in a relevant field and/or have expertise in a relevant methodology, as judged by their publication record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of conflicts of interest for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should ensure absence of conflicts of interest (e.g. recent collaboration with authors) for all peer reviewers; special attention should be given to reviewers suggested by authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of peer reviewers for primary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to obtain a minimum of two peer reviewers for manuscripts reporting primary research or secondary analysis of primary research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional circumstances (niche/emerging fields) it may not be possible to obtain two independent reviewers; Editors may decide to publish based on one report only if that report meets the standards set out (see peer review report quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review report quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports should be in English and provide constructive critical evaluations of the authors’ work, particularly regarding appropriateness of methods, accuracy of results, and whether conclusions are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions should be based on reviewer comments that meet these criteria rather than on short, superficial reports without rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of reviewer identity and use of institutional emails
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to independently verify the contact details of reviewers suggested by authors or other third parties; institutional email addresses should be used to invite reviewers wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each manuscript should be reviewed by at least one reviewer who was not suggested by the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of non-primary research content
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that do not report primary research (Editorials, Book Reviews, Commentaries, Opinion) may be accepted without two peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such manuscripts should be assessed by the Editor(s) if the topic is within their expertise; if not, they should be assessed by at least one independent expert reviewer or Editorial Board member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional manuscript handling and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to provide a professional service to authors; correspondence should be handled in a timely and professional manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangements should be in place so editorial staff absences do not reduce service. Editors should use the publisher’s online submission and peer-review system and maintain offline records as necessary to preserve a full record of peer review for each manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to respect and uphold the confidential status of materials submitted to the Journal and ensure that material remains confidential while under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Libelous or defamatory content
rubrics_metrics.description: If Editors believe a manuscript contains potentially libelous or defamatory content they are expected to seek advice from the Publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with field-specific ethical standards and editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must ensure manuscripts accepted comply with the Journal’s editorial policies and specific research requirements and ethics standards for the relevant field (e.g., human or animal research, endangered plants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, ensure compliance with international and comparable national ethics standards and seek advice from the Publisher in cases of uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, ethics approval and informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should be satisfied that all research involving human subjects, human material or human data accepted for publication is ethical and performed in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki or a comparable national standard; such research must comply with authors’ national and institutional ethics committee requirements for ethics approval and informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where research occurred in a different country, approval should be obtained from an ethics committee local to where the research took place. Manuscripts reporting human research should include a statement of independent ethics committee approval (naming the committee) and a statement of informed consent. If material might identify an individual, include a statement of informed consent to publish those details. In absence of local committees, use Declaration of Helsinki as standard and seek Publisher advice for difficult cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human tissue and stem cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving human tissue (including stem cells) should comply with national and international regulations and guidelines on the use of such tissue for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research appearing to violate relevant guidelines should be investigated according to COPE guidance and Publisher consulted in difficult cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research and endangered species standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Work reporting animal research should have approval from an appropriate ethics committee; research on endangered animal and plant species should comply with IUCN Policy and CITES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of an animal research ethics committee or guidelines, Editors should use discretion and seek Publisher advice in difficult cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should be aware of potential DURC issues relevant to their field and seek assistance from the Publisher if a manuscript presents information that can be directly misapplied to pose a significant threat to public health, safety, agriculture, environment, materials or security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Editors' conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to inform the Publisher of any interests that may influence, or be perceived to influence, their decisions; financial and non-financial interests should be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration does not disqualify Editors from the role, but Editors must respect confidentiality of peer review and editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling manuscripts authored by Editors or with Editor conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Editors may publish in their own journal, a senior Editorial Board member should be assigned to oversee peer review and decisions for any manuscript submitted and/or co-authored by the Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Board members must not be involved in peer review or decision-making for any manuscript on which they are an author or where they may have a conflict of interest. Editors submitting to the Journal must comply with the Journal’s author disclosure policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints, appeals and post-publication procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to have a written appeals and complaints procedure for the Journal and respond promptly to complaints (including anonymous, pseudonymous and named complainants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should, in collaboration with the Publisher, follow COPE flowcharts on whistleblowers; actionable complaints should be handled timely. Seek Publisher advice in difficult situations, particularly where retraction or expression of concern may be needed. Complaints against Editors will be investigated by the Publisher and may be referred to an independent ombudsman or COPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of the Publisher and media statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should not act as representatives of the Publisher or make statements to the media, post comments or write editorials claiming to represent the Publisher without the Publisher’s prior agreement.
